I just feel incredibly confused and overwhelmed by everything that is happening lately. It's more that I'm completely lost and can't explain why I act the way I do sometimes.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific times or situations when the voice you hear seems to be more prominent or louder, and how that relates to your feelings of being out of control or making poor decisions?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure if there are specific times when the voice gets louder or more prominent, as it seems to happen both when I'm alone in my apartment and in quiet boardrooms. While I can't clearly link its volume to specific decisions, its constant comments about me making a mess of the company definitely add to my overall feeling of losing control.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of significant emotional withdrawal or flatness, where you felt disconnected from your emotions or the world around you, beyond just feeling 'flat and blank' as you mentioned earlier?\n\nPatient: Yes, it goes much deeper than that—I've completely withdrawn from my life, ignoring calls from close friends and stopping activities I used to love like yoga and art gallery openings. While I haven't really noticed any specific speech issues like rambling, this overall sense of mental disorganization has been a significant struggle for me.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods where you believed the voice or the comments it made were coming from outside your mind, such as from the radio, TV, or other external sources, rather than just being a product of your own thoughts?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't ever experienced the voice coming from the TV, radio, or any other external media. It just sounds like a clear voice right there in the room with me, similar to a conference call, even though I know no one is actually there.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe that the voice you're hearing or the comments it makes are part of a plot against you, or that there's some other external force controlling your thoughts or actions?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think there is any kind of plot against me or some outside force controlling my mind. I just feel incredibly confused and overwhelmed by everything that is happening lately. It's more that I'm completely lost and can't explain why I act the way I do sometimes.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific times or situations when the voice you hear seems to be more prominent or louder, and how that relates to your feelings of being out of control or making poor decisions?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure if there are specific times when the voice gets louder or more prominent, as it seems to happen both when I'm alone in my apartment and in quiet boardrooms. While I can't clearly link its volume to specific decisions, its constant comments about me making a mess of the company definitely add to my overall feeling of losing control.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of significant emotional withdrawal or flatness, where you felt disconnected from your emotions or the world around you, beyond just feeling 'flat and blank' as you mentioned earlier?\n\nPatient: Yes, it goes much deeper than that—I've completely withdrawn from my life, ignoring calls from close friends and stopping activities I used to love like yoga and art gallery openings. It feels like the part of me that actually cared about anything has just quietly shut off. I mostly just sit on my couch doing absolutely nothing, sometimes even neglecting basic things like showering.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling like the part of you that actually cared about anything has 'quietly shut off', and how this affects your daily life and interactions with others?\n\nPatient: It means I don't feel any joy or drive anymore, so I just sit on the couch for hours doing absolutely nothing. I ignore calls from my team and close friends because trying to interact feels completely pointless, and I've stopped doing yoga, my art, or even showering. It's like my emotions have been completely emptied out, and I just can't bring myself to care.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you feel emotionally when the voice is commenting on your actions, and do you feel like you're able to distinguish between the voice's comments and your own thoughts and feelings?\n\nPatient: I'm not quite sure how to describe my emotions during those moments, other than feeling very overwhelmed. I also haven't really thought about how I distinguish the voice from my own thoughts, aside from knowing that there is physically no one in the room with me.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes of disorganized thinking or behavior that lasted for a shorter period, let's say less than a month, before returning to a more normal state, or have your symptoms been consistently present over the past three months?\n\nPatient: No, these haven't been short episodes that come and go. While my overall decline and struggle at work have been going on for over two years, the specific bizarre behaviors and the voice commenting on me have been a consistent, regular problem for roughly the last three months without returning to normal.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your motor behavior, such as catatonia or excessive and purposeless movement, alongside the voice and feelings of being out of control?\n\nPatient: Yes, I've had some very strange physical behaviors where I'll suddenly find myself standing completely still, staring at the office wall, or pacing up and down the hallways. I also laugh or snap at my team at completely inappropriate times. It deeply scares me because I have absolutely no explanation for why I am doing these things.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the progression of your symptoms over the past two years, including the decline in your work performance and the onset of the voice, has been gradual or if there were any specific events or times when your symptoms significantly worsened?\n\nPatient: The overall decline in my motivation and work performance started gradually about two and a half years ago, triggered by a high-stakes merger project. However, the more severe symptoms—like hearing the clear voice commenting on me and my highly erratic behavior at work—became a regular, prominent problem much more recently, over the last three months.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the voice you hear ever comments on your thoughts before you've said them out loud, or if it seems to know what you're thinking?"
  }

I don't think it comments on my thoughts or knows what I'm thinking, or at least I'm not sure about that. It really just seems to focus on commenting on my physical actions, like telling me I'm making a mess of the company or that people are laughing at what I'm doing.

Everything has been so overwhelming lately that it just feels incredibly frightening and confusing to experience.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice you hear interacts with you, for example, does it comment on your thoughts or actions, or does it have a conversation with you, and how does this impact your daily functioning and relationships?\n\nPatient: The voice doesn't converse with me, but rather acts as a clear man's voice—like someone on a conference call without video—commenting on my actions and telling me I'm making a mess of the company or that people are laughing at me. Because this has become so overwhelming and distracting, I've completely pulled away from my friends, ignored calls from my team, missed critical meetings, and even stopped doing yoga or keeping up with basic hygiene.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the voice you're hearing and the feelings of being out of control have been persistent over the past three months, or have they been episodic, and how have they affected your ability to function in daily life and maintain relationships?\n\nPatient: The voice and the feeling of losing control have been a regular, persistent problem for the last three months, rather than just coming and going. This, along with a general decline over the past two years, has severely disrupted my life—I've missed critical board meetings, nearly lost a key client, neglected basic hygiene, and pulled away from friends, leaving my spouse and the board highly concerned about my ability to function.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any significant difficulties with your thinking, such as trouble organizing your thoughts, or with your speech, like rambling or having trouble staying on topic, during these episodes or in general?\n\nPatient: Yes, over the past two years I've experienced a major slide in my thinking and ability to organize, which has led to me losing track of strategic documents and making erratic decisions that don't make sense to my team. While I haven't really noticed any specific speech issues like rambling, this overall sense of mental disorganization has been a significant struggle for me.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods where you believed the voice or the comments it made were coming from outside your mind, such as from the radio, TV, or other external sources, rather than just being a product of your own thoughts?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't ever experienced the voice coming from the TV, radio, or any other external media. It just sounds like a clear voice right there in the room with me, similar to a conference call, even though I know no one is actually there.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe that the voice you're hearing or the comments it makes are part of a plot against you, or that there's some other external force controlling your thoughts or actions?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think there is any kind of plot against me or some outside force controlling my mind. I just feel incredibly confused and overwhelmed by everything that is happening lately. It's more that I'm completely lost and can't explain why I act the way I do sometimes.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are any specific times or situations when the voice you hear seems to be more prominent or louder, and how that relates to your feelings of being out of control or making poor decisions?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure if there are specific times when the voice gets louder or more prominent, as it seems to happen both when I'm alone in my apartment and in quiet boardrooms. While I can't clearly link its volume to specific decisions, its constant comments about me making a mess of the company definitely add to my overall feeling of losing control.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of significant emotional withdrawal or flatness, where you felt disconnected from your emotions or the world around you, beyond just feeling 'flat and blank' as you mentioned earlier?\n\nPatient: Yes, it goes much deeper than that—I've completely withdrawn from my life, ignoring calls from close friends and stopping activities I used to love like yoga and art gallery openings. It feels like the part of me that actually cared about anything has just quietly shut off. I mostly just sit on my couch doing absolutely nothing, sometimes even neglecting basic things like showering.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling like the part of you that actually cared about anything has 'quietly shut off', and how this affects your daily life and interactions with others?\n\nPatient: It means I don't feel any joy or drive anymore, so I just sit on the couch for hours doing absolutely nothing.
